messages:
sam: hey team, first-week onboarding question. I built runtime from source but one of the unit tests keeps segfaulting when exercising the kv-cache. build succeeded, docker image runs, but test crashes. stack snippet below:

sam: ```
$ ./bazel-bin/runtime/tests/kv_cache_test --gtest_filter=KVCache.*
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
#0  0x7f8b2d4e1a in ?? () from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so.12.0
#1  0x55a3b6c3f4 in runtime::kv::Store::append(...)
#2  0x55a3b6c8a1 in main
```

sam: also ran `strace` quickly and I see a bunch of dlopen attempts failing for libnvidia-ml.so.1

mika: did you build with the system CUDA/toolkit that matches the node driver? which cuda version did you set in toolchain? :thinking:

sam: I used the default dev container from devex (cuda:12.2-base), `nvidia-smi` outputs fine though:

sam: ```
$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.86       Driver Version: 535.86       CUDA Version: 12.2     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

tiago: can you `ldd` the binary or the shared objects to see missing libs? often libnvidia-ml symlink is missing inside the container runtime causing dlopen failures even though nvidia-smi works on the host.

sam: ran ldd on the runtime shared object, here's the relevant lines:

sam: ```
$ ldd bazel-bin/runtime/libredwood_runtime.so | grep nvidia
libnvidia-ml.so.1 => not found
libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f8b2c900000)
```

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-472: "kv-cache segfault on dev container - libnvidia-ml missing" and assigned to infra oncall. More details: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-472 :ticket:

olivia: quick workaround you can try locally: if you have the libnvidia-ml file elsewhere in the container/runtime, create the symlink the process expects. Eg: `sudo ln -s /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.535.86 /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1` then re-run tests. if you're on k8s dev cluster ask infra to mount the driver libs into the pod.

sam: tried the symlink hack, `ldd` now resolves but test still segfaults with a slightly different backtrace:

sam: ```
#0  0x7fffa1b2e3 in nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex_v2 () from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1
#1  0x55a3b6c3f4 in runtime::gpu::DeviceTracker::init()
#2  0x55a3b6c8a1 in runtime::kv::Store::append
```

mika: hmm, OK. this smells like an ABI/driver mismatch or we hit an uninitialized pointer path where we call NVML too early. two quick things: 1) try `export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and run the test under `gdb` to get a full bt; 2) if you can, try switching the node image to driver 535 -> 535.* (matching lib version) or run the same image on a different dev gpu node. if the NVML call is returning weird values, infra ticket should be able to repro mount + driver pairing.

sam: will try gdb + blocking and report back. thanks for the quick leads :thumbsup:
